N-cone.objects: Real Banach spaces A0,A1, a nonnegative cone M+, its gauge, and strongly measurable A0-valued family F are specified in the fragment.
N-cone.domain: T>0 and 1<=p,q<=infinity are fixed. The allowed cases are q>1 or q=1 with finite p, excluding exactly (infinity,1).
N-cone.fixed_and_variable: A0->A1 and the spatial gauge constant C0 are fixed. Trajectories vary in F and cone membership is almost everywhere, not a pointwise assertion on chosen representatives.
N-cone.hypotheses: The injection is continuous and linear; the cone is nonnegatively scalable; its gauge is positive definite and degree one, dominates the A0 norm, and has compact bounded sets. Gauge measurability and A1-valued Bochner derivative bounds are explicit.
N-cone.equations: The gauge axioms and the combined uniform Lp(gauge)/Lq(A1 derivative) bound occur in the canonical text. Neither [u-v] nor a triangle inequality for the gauge is introduced.
N-cone.quantifiers: Every gauge-bounded sequence has an A0-convergent subsequence and one time bound holds uniformly for v in F. The conclusion does not require a single timewise compact set for untruncated values.
N-cone.conclusion: F is relatively compact in Lp(A0); infinity is included only for q>1. No membership of the limit in a nonclosed cone is inferred.
N-cone.status: Bounded-family form of Barrett--Suli arXiv1101.1990v2 Theorem 1 and Remark 2, pp.3--4, with strong measurability made explicit; independent local mechanism is expository, not original research.
N-cone.local_definitions: All cone axioms needed by this principal are repeated inside its own statement, so it can be read without an earlier definition node. The surrounding explanation warns against cone subtraction.

N-maitre.objects: E1,E2, compact nonlinear map K, bounded input family U and image family V={K(u)} are separately named in the actual fragment.
N-maitre.domain: Fixed T>0, target exponent 1<=p<=infinity, and an auxiliary 1<r<=infinity whose value is independent of p.
N-maitre.fixed_and_variable: K and the spaces are fixed. Each u varies in U, v=K(u) varies in V, and compactness is asserted only for V.
N-maitre.hypotheses: K sends bounded sets to relatively compact sets; U is L1 bounded; images are strongly measurable and belong to Lp; V has a uniform Lr bound and uniform target-Lp translations.
N-maitre.equations: The Lr supremum and target-Lp shift limit appear together. The later tail estimate retains K(0) and does not require K(0)=0.
N-maitre.quantifiers: There exists one r>1 and one uniform image bound for the whole family; the h-limit is uniform in v. This does not become pointwise time continuity alone.
N-maitre.conclusion: Strong compactness of K(u) in Lp for finite p, and compact continuous representatives for p=infinity. No compactness of u is asserted.
N-maitre.status: Imported published Maitre Theorem 2.1, p.1726, with renamed operator and explicit measurability. The original shifted sums are distinguished from the local convex-average reconstruction.
N-maitre.local_definitions: Compactness of K is defined by images of bounded sets, without silently assuming linearity, injectivity or monotonicity; translations are defined in adjoining notation.

N-simon.objects: The actual imported fragment specifies Banach spaces X,B,Y and a family F of Bochner Lp(X) trajectories.
N-simon.domain: Fixed finite interval (0,T), T>0, with every exponent 1<=p<=infinity explicitly allowed.
N-simon.fixed_and_variable: The embeddings and exponent are fixed, the functions vary in F, and compactness supplies subsequences rather than convergence of the whole family.
N-simon.hypotheses: X injects compactly into B and B injects continuously into Y; one uniform Lp(X) bound and a family-uniform Lp(Y) translation limit are both present.
N-simon.equations: The spatial supremum and the shortened-domain (0,T-h) translation expression occur literally in the canonical input; the adjoining prose keeps Y distinct from B.
N-simon.quantifiers: The supremum over all f in F precedes the h-down-to-zero limit, so a function-dependent modulus has not been substituted.
N-simon.conclusion: Finite-p conclusion is strong Lp(B) relative compactness. At infinity the conclusion is about B-valued continuous representatives in the supremum norm.
N-simon.status: Established imported result: Simon, journal Theorem 5, printed pp.84--85. No reflexivity or original theorem claim is added.
N-simon.local_definitions: The compact injection is identified in the claim; surrounding notation defines uniform translations and relative compactness. Bochner spaces are declared prerequisites.

Obtain compact interval integrals from t.finding: Holder bounds each interval integral by |I|^(1-1/p)M in X. The compact X->B and continuous B->Y injections give compact interval integrals in Y, where the separately assumed translations allow Simon Theorem 1, pp.71--73. This uses an interval integral, not a falsely uniform pointwise X bound.

Choose the Ehrling parameter before the.finding: The displayed Ehrling bound is applied to f_n-f_m in X and then Minkowski gives 2*eta*M. Fix eta<epsilon/(4M), then choose the Y-Cauchy indices; M=0 is treated separately. This reconstructs the upgrade in Simon Lemma 8/Theorem 5, pp.84--85, with the infinity representative claim explicitly imported.

Bound the exceptional-set measure and th.finding: Markov gives |G_M|<=C_U/M. On that set v-v_M=v-K(0); Holder supplies (C_U/M)^(1-1/r)C_V and the constant K(0) contributes the other term. The tail is uniform and L1 regardless of the target p; v_M is strongly measurable because it equals v off the measurable set and a constant on it. Source: Maitre Lemma 2.3, equations (2.3)--(2.10), pp.1726--1728.

Prove compactness of the closed convex h.finding: A finite delta-net for Q approximates every convex combination by the compact finite simplex; hence the convex hull is totally bounded and its closure is compact in the complete ambient Banach space. Measurable nearest-net cells approximate Bochner averages. The proof does not assert the average lies inside K(E1) or inside the cone. This is the displayed elementary reconstruction, not a quotation of Maitre shifted sums.

Transfer compactness to untruncated inte.finding: For fixed M the truncated values lie in the compact closure Q_M. Their interval integrals are compact by the earlier convex-average proof; choose M to reduce the tail and then a finite net. Thus the untruncated integrals are totally bounded and Simon applies with the actual Lp translations. The paragraph cites Maitre original Lemma 2.3, (2.3)--(2.24), pp.1726--1730 and labels the alternate proof route.

Derive a uniform supremum bound from W11.finding: Choosing an approximate average-norm time and integrating the Bochner derivative yields sup||v||<=T^-1||v||L1+||vprime||L1. The W11 fundamental theorem is an explicit prerequisite; no Banach Radon--Nikodym property is inferred from a merely Lipschitz function. Source interfaces: Simon Lemma 4, pp.77--78; Maitre Corollary 2.4, p.1730.

Use Fubini and bounded-amplitude interpo.finding: Fubini counts each derivative contribution for at most length h and gives hD in L1. Since the difference has amplitude at most 2K0, its pth power is bounded by (2K0)^(p-1) times its first power. The resulting h^(1/p) modulus tends to zero for every finite p, including p=1.

Use Holder for a supremum translation mo.finding: Holder on (t,t+h) gives h^(1-1/q)D; it is a small supremum modulus only for q>1, with q=infinity giving exponent one. At q=1 the written bound has exponent zero and cannot prove L-infinity translations. This is the exact distinction used later, consistent with Simon Corollary 4, pp.85--86.

Compute the ramp derivative bound and fi.finding: The ramp is continuous, nonnegative and bounded by one; its derivative equals n on an interval of length 1/n, so its L1 derivative norm is one. Substitution s=t-1/2 computes the finite-p error to the step as 1/(n*(p+1)). The example directly tests the excluded pair in Barrett--Suli Remark 2, p.4, and Simon Proposition 3, p.94.

Prove lack of L-infinity compactness fro.finding: Every subsequence has the same discontinuous pointwise step limit. If a subsequence were L-infinity convergent, the equality of essential-supremum and supremum norms for continuous differences would make it uniformly Cauchy; completeness would give a continuous uniform limit, contradicting that pointwise limit. The manuscript uses this actual obstruction rather than treating a failed estimate as a counterexample.

Calculate the pairwise L1 separation of.finding: For m>n, every fixed dyadic sign interval of level n splits into an even number of m intervals, half with each sign. The difference therefore has magnitude two on total measure one half, giving L1 distance one. K(x)=x^2 has compact images of bounded real sets and all images are constant one. This tests exactly Maitre Theorem 2.1/Remark 2.2(3), p.1726, and prevents a noninjective inverse-gauge transfer.

Normalize both cone points by the sum of.finding: Failure at eta0 selects a pair with a_n=[u_n]+[v_n]>0; scaling both by a_n produces two gauge-bounded sequences. Their A0-convergent common subsequence has A1 difference tending to zero because the normalized A0 difference stays bounded and is divided by n. The injective continuous inclusion forces equal limits, contradicting the eta0 separation. Only scaling of each point is used. Source: Barrett--Suli Lemma 1, pp.4--5.

Derive the A1 supremum bound and control.finding: The gauge domination and finite-interval Holder estimate put v in L1(A1); its assumed Lq derivative is also L1. W11 gives the written amplitude K1=C1*C0*T^(-1/p)G+T^(1-1/q)D. Markov on the scalar measurable gauge and that A1 amplitude give the 1/R tail, with cone membership used only almost everywhere. This is the local replacement for the unresolved source index-selection passage after (2.8), p.6, not an endorsement of that passage.

Obtain compact interval integrals and ap.finding: Gauge-truncated values lie in a compact A0 closure and hence a compact A1 closure. Compact convex averages plus the uniform L1 tail make every interior interval integral compact in A1. The manuscript uses finite-p interpolation for q=1 and the Holder supremum modulus for q>1, meeting every imported Simon Theorem 1 hypothesis in A1 before asserting the Cauchy subsequence.

Upgrade weak-space Cauchy convergence wi.finding: Pointwise two-point Ehrling and Minkowski give 2*eta*G+C_eta times the A1-Cauchy difference. Eta is fixed before the indices; G=0 is explicit. The infinity representative extension uses a full-measure dense good-time set, then completeness and injectivity. This is the final upgrade of Barrett--Suli equation (2.22), pp.12--13, after a separately reconstructed weak-space argument, with the scoped source concern disclosed.

Construct the degree-one inverse gauge a.finding: Injectivity and positive homogeneity make K(0)=0 and K^-1(cv)=c^(1/alpha)K^-1(v); hence [v]=||K^-1v||^alpha is a positive degree-one gauge. Compact image of the unit ball gives a uniform bound, which scales to ||Kx||<=C||x||^alpha. Gauge-bounded sets are compact images of bounded input sets. Source interface: Barrett--Suli Section 4, pp.15--16.

Compute the inverse-lift L1 bound and th.finding: The displayed Holder bound is T^(1-1/(alpha*p))*G^(1/alpha), with alpha*p>=1; the infinity case has factor T. Strongly measurable inverse lifts are assumed separately rather than inferred from injectivity. Gauge domination and the E2 derivative bound yield uniform W11(E2), hence every fixed auxiliary Lr(E2), r>1.

Check matching derivative and output spa.finding: Both the derivative and output space here are E2. The finite-p or supremum translation estimate therefore matches Maitre Theorem 2.1, p.1726. For q>1 the W11 amplitude also puts V in L-infinity and its supremum translations allow the continuous compactness conclusion even if the original gauge exponent was finite. The following paragraph forbids substituting a derivative only in a larger weak space or assuming every cone has this parametrization.
